summary: I wrote src/main.ts. It builds a 600×600 ground plane and three InstancedMesh objects: 8,000 trunks, 8,000 canopies and 2,000 rocks. That makes 10,000 scattered objects, with no per-object meshes. Placement uses a seeded mulberry32 generator, so the forest is the same on every load. Canopies, trunks and rocks each get a per-instance colour through setColorAt. The scene has one shadow-casting directional light (4096 shadow map), a weak hemisphere fill light, and FogExp2. The camera orbits slowly at radius 105 and height 62, looking at the centre, so the whole 130×130 forest stays in view. The render loop uses requestAnimationFrame and sets `window.__EVAL_READY__` after the first frame. The typecheck passes. I did not run `vite build` or view the scene in a browser, so the look of the shadows and fog is untested.
